messages.author: 2060c8e54fb73471
messages.subject: Can factor variance be "too small"?
parts:
Good evening, 
I have a first order factor with a variance not significally different from 0 (when estimated using predict(), the factor variance is around .0001).

Can this be the cause of problems I experience in more complex models, when I estimate covariance between this and other latent factors, or I model second order factors?

What usually happens is that I obtain estimated correlations greater than 1 and/or a non-positive definite covariance matrix of latent variables...

Thanks in advance to anyone able to shed some light on this

Federica

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Can factor variance be "too small"?
parts: the factor variance is around .0001

Is that small relative to the scale of your indicators?  If factor variance is nearly zero, it could indicate there is very little in common among the indicators.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 2060c8e54fb73471
messages.subject: Re: Can factor variance be "too small"?
parts:
Dear Terrence,

Thank you, and sorry for the late reply.

Meanwhile, I learnt that I misused the predict function, because there are missing data in my model*. Therefore, .0001 might not be a good estimation of the factor variance. To answer you question, however, yes, it would be very small compared to the scale of my indicators, which have a mean around 14 and SD around 2.7

The model is a linear latent growth curve model estimated over 5 timepoints, and the factor with non-significant variance is the slope. When I first looked over the data, I did not notice anything peculiar, such as extremely uniform or extremely "un-uniform" change trajectories, I am now trying to look into it more accurately.
* there are missing data because of participants' dropout over time, and I used FIML to handle this

Best,
Federica Conte
